<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Serve [`LiquidAI/d1-3B`](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/d1-3B) on `/v1/systemone` with answers that match the checkpoint's own `model.system_one()`, for text and image states.

The question types (#60696) and the `images` request field (#61064) have since landed on `main`, so this PR is now only the Liquid read strategy and the small changes to the next-token read that it needs.

```bash
vllm serve LiquidAI/d1-3B
```

## Demo

d1-3B playing Snake through `/v1/systemone`, recorded in real time on one B300. Each move is one HTTP request with a single `choice` question (up / down / left / right), and the snake takes the model's top choice with no fallback logic.

![d1-3B playing Snake on vLLM](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mgoin/vllm/pr-60676-assets/d1_snake.gif)

In this 15 second run it made 666 moves (44 a second, 23 ms median per request), ate 46 apples and died once. The state is a short text: where the apple is relative to the head, and what is in each of the four neighboring cells. Given raw coordinates or an ASCII grid instead, the model played poorly (14 and 4 apples in 400 moves, against 32). The recording used the default prefix caching; see Details for why turning it off is faster here.

## Claims

- d1-3B picks and probabilities on `/v1/systemone` match the reference implementation shipped with the checkpoint, for text and image states and all three question types.
- Images are fetched once per request and shrunk to at most 1024 x 1024 pixels, as the reference does.
- A read that fails after rendering an image no longer breaks the next request that uses the same image.

## Validation

**Prompt parity (CPU).** For 15 questions over 11 cases, the rendered prompt and the label token ids are identical to what `prompt.py` in the d1-3B repo produces (`render` and `readout_ids`).

**Answers against the reference (one B300, bf16).** Reference: `AutoModel.from_pretrained("LiquidAI/d1-3B", trust_remote_code=True).system_one(...)` on transformers 5.18.0, each question asked alone. "Gap" is the largest absolute difference in any option's probability.

| Case | vLLM | Reference | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ticket, 3 questions (noul / choice / score) | 0.990 / billing / 0.757 | 0.990 / billing / 0.757 | 0.0007 |
| Single choice | technical | technical | 0.0008 |
| Single noul | 0.018 | 0.020 | 0.0023 |
| Single score, 3 levels | 1.817 | 1.823 | 0.0032 |
| JSON state, 2 questions | billing / 0.349 | billing / 0.349 | < 0.0001 |
| Japanese text in a JSON state | Japanese | Japanese | 0.031 |
| Noul with criteria | 0.982 | 0.982 | < 0.0001 |
| Options named `a` to `d` | b | b | 0.0002 |
| Score, 10 levels | 7.373 | 7.373 | < 0.0001 |
| Image only (COCO 000000039769), 1 question | two | two | 0.0005 |
| Image and text, 2 questions | two / 0.984 | two / 0.986 | 0.0019 |

Every pick matches. The Japanese case has the same prompt tokens and the same pick; its distribution is spread over three options (0.33 / 0.51 / 0.16). I did not track down the source of that 0.031 gap.

**Reviewer findings (thanks @simon-veitner-redhat).** All five are addressed, re-implemented on the current `main` and re-checked on a B300:

| Finding | Now |
|---|---|
| A decision that fails after rendering an image breaks the next request with that image | Renders skip the sender cache. A failing two-question image request returns 400, and a chat request and a decision with the same image then return 200. |
| Each question fetches every image again | Images are fetched once and passed to every question. |
| Images above 1 MP differ from `system_one()` | Shrunk as the reference does. A 1280x960 image gives the same 1814 input tokens and probabilities within 0.0019. |
| A one-letter option name that is several tokens fails with a `max()` error | Returns 400 naming the label. |
| `confidence` differs from `system_one()` | Left as vLLM's definition. The docs now claim only picks and probabilities. |

**Tests.**

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions tests/entrypoints/generate/generative_scoring
```

72 passed on a B300, on this branch as pushed.

**Not covered in CI.** There is no d1-3B end-to-end test, to avoid pulling a 3B checkpoint. The d1 prompt wording is pinned by a CPU-only unit test; the answer parity above was run by hand.

## Details

- **Why a strategy.** d1 is a post-trained LFM2.5-VL-3B that expects a fixed prompt (`QUESTION:` / `Options:` / `Reply with the option code only.`) and pools label variants (`yes`/`Yes`/`YES`, `A`/` A`). `LiquidStrategy` subclasses `NextTokenStrategy` and overrides only the user turn and the label tokens.
- **Label groups.** A read now takes a group of tokens per label and scores the best one. The generic strategy uses groups of one, so its behavior is unchanged.
- **Selected by architecture.** d1's `config.json` is the same as the base model's, so every `Lfm2VlForConditionalGeneration` gets this prompt. Liquid's runner does the same.
- **Usage.** `input_tokens` sums the prompt of every question, so a multi-question request reports more than the reference, which counts the state once.
- **Limitations.** A `choice` is still capped at 26 options (the reference switches to two-digit codes beyond that). An empty-string state is treated like a `null` state.
- **Latency.** On one B300 a single-question request takes about 14 ms: roughly 9 ms in the engine step, 3 ms between the API server and the engine, and 1 ms each for HTTP and for rendering the prompt. With prefix caching on (the default) and a state that changes every request, the median rises to 22 ms and is bimodal (14 / 22 / 31 ms); `--no-enable-prefix-caching` brings it back to a flat 14 ms. I did not trace the cause in the scheduler.
- **Overlap.** Not a duplicate: no other open PR serves d1.
- **Shared changes.** The media connector moves from `JointSchemaStrategy` to the `ReadStrategy` base so both strategies use it, and every next-token render now skips the multimodal sender cache.

Hi @mgoin, I ran an adversarial pass on the d1 strategy on an H200. The prompt and readout hold up: every pick matched `model.system_one()` on 27 text and image cases, and with both sides in fp32 the probabilities agree within 0.0003 (the bf16 gaps, including the Japanese 0.031, are single bf16 logit steps). Tests pass (56/56). The image path has three bugs, plus two smaller items. The fixes are four commits on [`pr60676-review-fixes`](https://github.com/simon-veitner-redhat/vllm/tree/pr60676-review-fixes), based on this PR's head, each cherry-pickable on its own. All repros were re-run on that branch and now behave as expected. ### 1. A failed or overlapping decision breaks the next request with the same image (chat included) `read()` renders all questions before sending any. The first render marks the image as sent in the mm sender cache (P0). If a later question fails (e.g. an 11-level score, L285), nothing reaches the engine, and the next request with those image bytes sends only the hash and hits a P1 cache miss. A request that arrives while a long decision is still rendering fails the same way. Fix: render with `skip_mm_cache=True`, as the render-only endpoints do: https://github.com/simon-veitner-redhat/vllm/commit/d11e50c847decf90ae71ca0d25bc6dc494d0ded2
Repro (failed request), vllm serve LiquidAI/d1-3B --port 18676, same on any Lfm2Vl model ```python # Server: vllm serve LiquidAI/d1-3B --port 18676 (also any Lfm2Vl model, e.g. LFM2-VL-450M) # A decision request that fails after rendering question 1 poisons the image cache; # the next chat completion with the same image then fails with 500. import base64, json, os, struct, urllib.request, zlib URL, M = f"http://127.0.0.1:{os.environ.get('PORT', '18676')}", os.environ.get("MODEL", "LiquidAI/d1-3B") raw = b"".join(b"\0" + os.urandom(3 * 32) for _ in range(32)) # fresh 32x32 noise PNG each run ch = lambda t, d: struct.pack(">I", len(d)) + t + d + struct.pack(">I", zlib.crc32(t + d)) img = "data:image/png;base64," + base64.b64encode(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n" + ch(b"IHDR", struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", 32, 32, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)) + ch(b"IDAT", zlib.compress(raw)) + ch(b"IEND", b"")).decode() def post(path, body): try: r = urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(URL + path, json.dumps(body).encode(), {"Content-Type": "application/json"})); return r.status, r.read()[:160] except urllib.error.HTTPError as e: return e.code, e.read()[:160] if not os.environ.get("CONTROL"): print("decision:", post("/v1/systemone", {"model": M, "state": "x", "images": [img], "questions": { "a": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Red?"}, "b": {"type": "score", "instructions": "Rate.", "criteria": list("0123456789X")}}})) print("chat: ", post("/v1/chat/completions", {"model": M, "max_tokens": 1, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": img}}, {"type": "text", "text": "Color?"}]}]})) ``` Observed (d1-3B): `decision: 400 (at most 10 levels)`, then `chat: 500 Internal server error` (log: "Multi-modal cache miss ... P0/P1 cache drift"). Expected: chat 200, as it is without the failed decision first (`CONTROL=1`).
Repro (overlapping request, no failure) ```python # Server: vllm serve LiquidAI/d1-3B --port 18676 (also LFM2-VL-450M) # Request A: 64 questions over one image (64 renders before anything reaches the engine). # Request B: one question over the same image, sent 0.3 s later -> fails (no failed request involved). import base64, io, json, os, threading, time, urllib.request from PIL import Image URL, M = f"http://127.0.0.1:{os.environ.get('PORT', '18676')}", os.environ.get("MODEL", "LiquidAI/d1-3B") buf = io.BytesIO(); Image.frombytes("RGB", (1024, 1024), os.urandom(3 << 20)).save(buf, "PNG") img = "data:image/png;base64," + base64.b64encode(buf.getvalue()).decode() def post(tag, n): body = {"model": M, "state": "x", "images": [img], "questions": {f"q{i}": {"type": "noul", "instructions": f"Q{i}?"} for i in range(n)}} t = time.time() try: r = urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(URL + "/v1/systemone", json.dumps(body).encode(), {"Content-Type": "application/json"})); s, b = r.status, r.read() except urllib.error.HTTPError as e: s, b = e.code, e.read() print(tag, s, f"{time.time() - t:.2f}s", b[:110]) a = threading.Thread(target=post, args=("A (64 q):", 64)); a.start(); time.sleep(0.3); post("B (1 q): ", 1); a.join() ``` Observed: `B (1 q): 400 Generation error for item 0` in 4 of 4 runs (1 on d1-3B, 3 on LFM2-VL-450M); A 200. Expected: both 200.
### 2. Each question fetches every image again Every render builds its own media connector, so N questions fetch, decode and hash each image N times, one after another, and a URL with changing content gives the questions different pictures. Fix: fetch once with the chat path's media rules and pass the decoded images to every question: https://github.com/simon-veitner-redhat/vllm/commit/8ca898731af7ca2d0c790bee2275155d55c5fde4
Repro, vllm serve LiquidAI/d1-3B --port 18676, same on any Lfm2Vl model ```python # Server: vllm serve LiquidAI/d1-3B --port 18676 (also LFM2-VL-450M) # One request, 2 identical questions, 1 image URL. The URL serves red then blue (a live snapshot). # Each question fetches the image again, so the two identical questions see different pictures. import io, json, os, threading, urllib.request from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer from PIL import Image URL, M = f"http://127.0.0.1:{os.environ.get('PORT', '18676')}", os.environ.get("MODEL", "LiquidAI/d1-3B") def png(c): b = io.BytesIO(); Image.new("RGB", (64, 64), c).save(b, "PNG"); return b.getvalue() imgs, gets = [png((230, 20, 20)), png((20, 20, 230))], [] class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler): def do_GET(self): body = imgs[len(gets) % 2]; gets.append(1) self.send_response(200); self.send_header("Content-Type", "image/png"); self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body))); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(body) def log_message(self, *a): pass srv = HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), H); threading.Thread(target=srv.serve_forever, daemon=True).start() q = {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Is the image red?"} body = {"model": M, "state": None, "images": [f"http://127.0.0.1:{srv.server_port}/x.png"], "questions": {"q1": q, "q2": q}} r = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(URL + "/v1/systemone", json.dumps(body).encode(), {"Content-Type": "application/json"}))) print("image GETs:", len(gets), "| P(red) q1 =", round(r["answers"]["q1"]["noul"], 3), "q2 =", round(r["answers"]["q2"]["noul"], 3)) ``` Observed (d1-3B): `image GETs: 2 | P(red) q1 = 0.986 q2 = 0.02`. Expected: `image GETs: 1` and the same answer for both questions.
### 3. Images above 1 MP give different answers from `system_one()` d1's `runner.py` shrinks every picture to at most 1024×1024 px (bicubic) before the processor; here it goes in as sent, so the tile grid and the pixels differ. Same commit as 2 (`LiquidStrategy.max_image_pixels`).
Repro, vllm serve LiquidAI/d1-3B --port 18676, img/cat03.jpg = Wikimedia Commons Cat03.jpg ```python # Server: vllm serve LiquidAI/d1-3B --port 18676 # The same photo sent as-is (1600x1598) and downscaled to 1 MP the way d1's runner.cap_pixels does. # model.system_one() always sees the 1 MP version, so only the second row matches the reference. import base64, io, json, math, os, sys, urllib.request from PIL import Image URL = f"http://127.0.0.1:{os.environ.get('PORT', '18676')}/v1/systemone" im = Image.open(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "img/cat03.jpg").convert("RGB") s = math.sqrt(1024 * 1024 / (im.width * im.height)) for tag, pic in [("as sent ", im), ("1MP-capped", im.resize((int(im.width * s), int(im.height * s)), Image.Resampling.BICUBIC))]: b = io.BytesIO(); pic.save(b, "PNG") body = {"model": "LiquidAI/d1-3B", "state": None, "images": ["data:image/png;base64," + base64.b64encode(b.getvalue()).decode()], "questions": {"indoor": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Is the photo taken indoors?"}}} r = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(URL, json.dumps(body).encode(), {"Content-Type": "application/json"}))) print(tag, pic.size, "P(indoor) =", round(r["answers"]["indoor"]["noul"], 4), "input_tokens =", r["usage"]["input_tokens"]) ``` Observed: as sent `P(indoor) = 0.1824`, 2578 tokens; capped `0.0953`, 1293 tokens. Expected: `system_one()` on the same file gives `0.0953` with 1293 tokens. In fp32 a 3840×2880 photo flips a yes/no answer (0.454 vs 0.551).
### 4. A one-letter option name that is several tokens fails with a `max()` error `"丙".isalpha()` is True, so 丙 becomes a code; 丙 and " 丙" are both multi-token, the group is `[]`, and the check (L305) compares `[]` with `ids[:1] == []` and passes. Fix (one line, `not ids or`): https://github.com/simon-veitner-redhat/vllm/commit/fee6ea22a6027cd228fc64d8a54f28efdf1c6c51
Repro, vllm serve LiquidAI/d1-3B --port 18676 ```bash # 丙 is one letter (isalpha) but two d1 tokens -> empty label group. curl -s -w '\nHTTP %{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:${PORT:-18676}/v1/systemone -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"LiquidAI/d1-3B","state":"Average quality.","questions":{"g":{"type":"choice","instructions":"Grade?","criteria":{"甲":"good","丙":"average"}}}}' ``` Observed: `400 "max() iterable argument is empty"`. Expected: the intended `400 "label '丙' is not one distinct token for this model"` (`system_one()` answers, using fallback code `A`).
### 5. `confidence` does not match `system_one()` The reference returns `probs[best]`; here it is `probs[top] * label_mass`, with `label_mass` summing every pooled variant. Picks and probabilities match; `confidence` is 0.004–0.020 lower on d1. Keeping one definition across models seems fine; the commit narrows the docs claim to picks and probabilities: https://github.com/simon-veitner-redhat/vllm/commit/37609180281ecb0079c9c9b833b1c0cc5bf169e3
Repro, vllm serve LiquidAI/d1-3B --port 18676 ```bash # The reference's choice confidence is max(probabilities); vLLM returns max(probabilities) * label_mass. curl -s http://127.0.0.1:${PORT:-18676}/v1/systemone -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"'${MODEL:-LiquidAI/d1-3B}'","state":"I was charged twice this month, please refund one of them.","questions":{"team":{"type":"choice","instructions":"Which team should handle this?","criteria":{"billing":"Charges, refunds, invoices","technical":"App or site faults","fraud":"Suspected unauthorised use"}}}}' \ | jq -c '{confidence: .answers.team.confidence, max_prob: ([.answers.team.probabilities[]]|max), label_mass: .diagnostics.team.label_mass, max_prob_x_mass: (([.answers.team.probabilities[]]|max) * .diagnostics.team.label_mass)}' ``` Observed: `{"confidence":0.97587,"max_prob":0.98423,"label_mass":0.99150}`. Expected (`system_one()`, same input): `confidence 0.98286`, its max probability.
### Run-to-run variance (fixed separately) Under concurrent load a label's bf16 logit moves by one step, so near-ties flip: the Japanese case picks English in about half of loaded runs. Computing the lm_head in fp32 removes this at no measured cost (322 vs 324 req/s at 32 in flight), but `--hf-overrides '{"head_dtype": "float32"}'` is ignored for multimodal models today; I will send that as a separate [Bugfix] PR. Until then `--hf-overrides '{"text_config": {"head_dtype": "float32"}}'` works.
Repro, vllm serve LiquidAI/d1-3B --port 18676 ```python # Server: vllm serve LiquidAI/d1-3B --port 18676 (bf16, default prefix caching) # The PR's Japanese case asked alone, then 32 times mixed with 32 other requests, 32 in flight. # Batch shape moves one label logit by one bf16 step: Japanese 0.3985 / English 0.3744 becomes # a 0.3837 tie, and argmax picks English. import collections, json, os, random, urllib.request from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor URL = f"http://127.0.0.1:{os.environ.get('PORT', '18676')}/v1/systemone" LANG = {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Which language is the message in?", "criteria": {"English": None, "Japanese": None, "Chinese": None}} JA = {"model": "LiquidAI/d1-3B", "state": {"message": "注文した商品がまだ届きません。返金してください。"}, "questions": {"lang": LANG}} def other(i): # a different request with a random-length state return {"model": "LiquidAI/d1-3B", "state": "refund order crash " * random.Random(i).choice([5, 50, 300]), "questions": {"d": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Angry?"}}} def ask(body): r = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(URL, json.dumps(body).encode(), {"Content-Type": "application/json"}))) a = r["answers"].get("lang") return a and (a["choice"], round(a["probabilities"]["Japanese"], 4), round(a["probabilities"]["English"], 4)) print("alone:", ask(JA)) jobs = [JA] * 32 + [other(i) for i in range(32)] random.Random(0).shuffle(jobs) with ThreadPoolExecutor(32) as ex: print("mixed:", collections.Counter(a for a in ex.map(ask, jobs) if a)) ``` Observed: `alone: ('Japanese', 0.3985, 0.3744)`, `mixed: Counter({('Japanese', 0.3985, 0.3744): 17, ('English', 0.3837, 0.3837): 15})`. Expected: all 32 equal to the answer asked alone (with the fp32 head, all 32 pick Japanese).

detail.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Serve [`LiquidAI/d1-3B`](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/d1-3B) on `/v1/systemone` with answers that match the checkpoint's own `model.system_one()`, for text and image states.

The question types (#60696) and the `images` request field (#61064) have since landed on `main`, so this PR is now only the Liquid read strategy and the small changes to the next-token read that it needs.

```bash
vllm serve LiquidAI/d1-3B
```

## Demo

d1-3B playing Snake through `/v1/systemone`, recorded in real time on one B300. Each move is one HTTP request with a single `choice` question (up / down / left / right), and the snake takes the model's top choice with no fallback logic.

![d1-3B playing Snake on vLLM](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mgoin/vllm/pr-60676-assets/d1_snake.gif)

In this 15 second run it made 666 moves (44 a second, 23 ms median per request), ate 46 apples and died once. The state is a short text: where the apple is relative to the head, and what is in each of the four neighboring cells. Given raw coordinates or an ASCII grid instead, the model played poorly (14 and 4 apples in 400 moves, against 32). The recording used the default prefix caching; see Details for why turning it off is faster here.

## Claims

- d1-3B picks and probabilities on `/v1/systemone` match the reference implementation shipped with the checkpoint, for text and image states and all three question types.
- Images are fetched once per request and shrunk to at most 1024 x 1024 pixels, as the reference does.
- A read that fails after rendering an image no longer breaks the next request that uses the same image.

## Validation

**Prompt parity (CPU).** For 15 questions over 11 cases, the rendered prompt and the label token ids are identical to what `prompt.py` in the d1-3B repo produces (`render` and `readout_ids`).

**Answers against the reference (one B300, bf16).** Reference: `AutoModel.from_pretrained("LiquidAI/d1-3B", trust_remote_code=True).system_one(...)` on transformers 5.18.0, each question asked alone. "Gap" is the largest absolute difference in any option's probability.

| Case | vLLM | Reference | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ticket, 3 questions (noul / choice / score) | 0.990 / billing / 0.757 | 0.990 / billing / 0.757 | 0.0007 |
| Single choice | technical | technical | 0.0008 |
| Single noul | 0.018 | 0.020 | 0.0023 |
| Single score, 3 levels | 1.817 | 1.823 | 0.0032 |
| JSON state, 2 questions | billing / 0.349 | billing / 0.349 | < 0.0001 |
| Japanese text in a JSON state | Japanese | Japanese | 0.031 |
| Noul with criteria | 0.982 | 0.982 | < 0.0001 |
| Options named `a` to `d` | b | b | 0.0002 |
| Score, 10 levels | 7.373 | 7.373 | < 0.0001 |
| Image only (COCO 000000039769), 1 question | two | two | 0.0005 |
| Image and text, 2 questions | two / 0.984 | two / 0.986 | 0.0019 |

Every pick matches. The Japanese case has the same prompt tokens and the same pick; its distribution is spread over three options (0.33 / 0.51 / 0.16). I did not track down the source of that 0.031 gap.

**Reviewer findings (thanks @simon-veitner-redhat).** All five are addressed, re-implemented on the current `main` and re-checked on a B300:

| Finding | Now |
|---|---|
| A decision that fails after rendering an image breaks the next request with that image | Renders skip the sender cache. A failing two-question image request returns 400, and a chat request and a decision with the same image then return 200. |
| Each question fetches every image again | Images are fetched once and passed to every question. |
| Images above 1 MP differ from `system_one()` | Shrunk as the reference does. A 1280x960 image gives the same 1814 input tokens and probabilities within 0.0019. |
| A one-letter option name that is several tokens fails with a `max()` error | Returns 400 naming the label. |
| `confidence` differs from `system_one()` | Left as vLLM's definition. The docs now claim only picks and probabilities. |

**Tests.**

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions tests/entrypoints/generate/generative_scoring
```

72 passed on a B300, on this branch as pushed.

**Not covered in CI.** There is no d1-3B end-to-end test, to avoid pulling a 3B checkpoint. The d1 prompt wording is pinned by a CPU-only unit test; the answer parity above was run by hand.

## Details

- **Why a strategy.** d1 is a post-trained LFM2.5-VL-3B that expects a fixed prompt (`QUESTION:` / `Options:` / `Reply with the option code only.`) and pools label variants (`yes`/`Yes`/`YES`, `A`/` A`). `LiquidStrategy` subclasses `NextTokenStrategy` and overrides only the user turn and the label tokens.
- **Label groups.** A read now takes a group of tokens per label and scores the best one. The generic strategy uses groups of one, so its behavior is unchanged.
- **Selected by architecture.** d1's `config.json` is the same as the base model's, so every `Lfm2VlForConditionalGeneration` gets this prompt. Liquid's runner does the same.
- **Usage.** `input_tokens` sums the prompt of every question, so a multi-question request reports more than the reference, which counts the state once.
- **Limitations.** A `choice` is still capped at 26 options (the reference switches to two-digit codes beyond that). An empty-string state is treated like a `null` state.
- **Latency.** On one B300 a single-question request takes about 14 ms: roughly 9 ms in the engine step, 3 ms between the API server and the engine, and 1 ms each for HTTP and for rendering the prompt. With prefix caching on (the default) and a state that changes every request, the median rises to 22 ms and is bimodal (14 / 22 / 31 ms); `--no-enable-prefix-caching` brings it back to a flat 14 ms. I did not trace the cause in the scheduler.
- **Overlap.** Not a duplicate: no other open PR serves d1.
- **Shared changes.** The media connector moves from `JointSchemaStrategy` to the `ReadStrategy` base so both strategies use it, and every next-token render now skips the multimodal sender cache.

Hi @mgoin, I ran an adversarial pass on the d1 strategy on an H200. The prompt and readout hold up: every pick matched `model.system_one()` on 27 text and image cases, and with both sides in fp32 the probabilities agree within 0.0003 (the bf16 gaps, including the Japanese 0.031, are single bf16 logit steps). Tests pass (56/56). The image path has three bugs, plus two smaller items. The fixes are four commits on [`pr60676-review-fixes`](https://github.com/simon-veitner-redhat/vllm/tree/pr60676-review-fixes), based on this PR's head, each cherry-pickable on its own. All repros were re-run on that branch and now behave as expected. ### 1. A failed or overlapping decision breaks the next request with the same image (chat included) `read()` renders all questions before sending any. The first render marks the image as sent in the mm sender cache (P0). If a later question fails (e.g. an 11-level score, L285), nothing reaches the engine, and the next request with those image bytes sends only the hash and hits a P1 cache miss. A request that arrives while a long decision is still rendering fails the same way. Fix: render with `skip_mm_cache=True`, as the render-only endpoints do: https://github.com/simon-veitner-redhat/vllm/commit/d11e50c847decf90ae71ca0d25bc6dc494d0ded2
Repro (failed request), vllm serve LiquidAI/d1-3B --port 18676, same on any Lfm2Vl model ```python # Server: vllm serve LiquidAI/d1-3B --port 18676 (also any Lfm2Vl model, e.g. LFM2-VL-450M) # A decision request that fails after rendering question 1 poisons the image cache; # the next chat completion with the same image then fails with 500. import base64, json, os, struct, urllib.request, zlib URL, M = f"http://127.0.0.1:{os.environ.get('PORT', '18676')}", os.environ.get("MODEL", "LiquidAI/d1-3B") raw = b"".join(b"\0" + os.urandom(3 * 32) for _ in range(32)) # fresh 32x32 noise PNG each run ch = lambda t, d: struct.pack(">I", len(d)) + t + d + struct.pack(">I", zlib.crc32(t + d)) img = "data:image/png;base64," + base64.b64encode(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n" + ch(b"IHDR", struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", 32, 32, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)) + ch(b"IDAT", zlib.compress(raw)) + ch(b"IEND", b"")).decode() def post(path, body): try: r = urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(URL + path, json.dumps(body).encode(), {"Content-Type": "application/json"})); return r.status, r.read()[:160] except urllib.error.HTTPError as e: return e.code, e.read()[:160] if not os.environ.get("CONTROL"): print("decision:", post("/v1/systemone", {"model": M, "state": "x", "images": [img], "questions": { "a": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Red?"}, "b": {"type": "score", "instructions": "Rate.", "criteria": list("0123456789X")}}})) print("chat: ", post("/v1/chat/completions", {"model": M, "max_tokens": 1, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": img}}, {"type": "text", "text": "Color?"}]}]})) ``` Observed (d1-3B): `decision: 400 (at most 10 levels)`, then `chat: 500 Internal server error` (log: "Multi-modal cache miss ... P0/P1 cache drift"). Expected: chat 200, as it is without the failed decision first (`CONTROL=1`).
Repro (overlapping request, no failure) ```python # Server: vllm serve LiquidAI/d1-3B --port 18676 (also LFM2-VL-450M) # Request A: 64 questions over one image (64 renders before anything reaches the engine). # Request B: one question over the same image, sent 0.3 s later -> fails (no failed request involved). import base64, io, json, os, threading, time, urllib.request from PIL import Image URL, M = f"http://127.0.0.1:{os.environ.get('PORT', '18676')}", os.environ.get("MODEL", "LiquidAI/d1-3B") buf = io.BytesIO(); Image.frombytes("RGB", (1024, 1024), os.urandom(3 << 20)).save(buf, "PNG") img = "data:image/png;base64," + base64.b64encode(buf.getvalue()).decode() def post(tag, n): body = {"model": M, "state": "x", "images": [img], "questions": {f"q{i}": {"type": "noul", "instructions": f"Q{i}?"} for i in range(n)}} t = time.time() try: r = urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(URL + "/v1/systemone", json.dumps(body).encode(), {"Content-Type": "application/json"})); s, b = r.status, r.read() except urllib.error.HTTPError as e: s, b = e.code, e.read() print(tag, s, f"{time.time() - t:.2f}s", b[:110]) a = threading.Thread(target=post, args=("A (64 q):", 64)); a.start(); time.sleep(0.3); post("B (1 q): ", 1); a.join() ``` Observed: `B (1 q): 400 Generation error for item 0` in 4 of 4 runs (1 on d1-3B, 3 on LFM2-VL-450M); A 200. Expected: both 200.
### 2. Each question fetches every image again Every render builds its own media connector, so N questions fetch, decode and hash each image N times, one after another, and a URL with changing content gives the questions different pictures. Fix: fetch once with the chat path's media rules and pass the decoded images to every question: https://github.com/simon-veitner-redhat/vllm/commit/8ca898731af7ca2d0c790bee2275155d55c5fde4
Repro, vllm serve LiquidAI/d1-3B --port 18676, same on any Lfm2Vl model ```python # Server: vllm serve LiquidAI/d1-3B --port 18676 (also LFM2-VL-450M) # One request, 2 identical questions, 1 image URL. The URL serves red then blue (a live snapshot). # Each question fetches the image again, so the two identical questions see different pictures. import io, json, os, threading, urllib.request from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer from PIL import Image URL, M = f"http://127.0.0.1:{os.environ.get('PORT', '18676')}", os.environ.get("MODEL", "LiquidAI/d1-3B") def png(c): b = io.BytesIO(); Image.new("RGB", (64, 64), c).save(b, "PNG"); return b.getvalue() imgs, gets = [png((230, 20, 20)), png((20, 20, 230))], [] class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler): def do_GET(self): body = imgs[len(gets) % 2]; gets.append(1) self.send_response(200); self.send_header("Content-Type", "image/png"); self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body))); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(body) def log_message(self, *a): pass srv = HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), H); threading.Thread(target=srv.serve_forever, daemon=True).start() q = {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Is the image red?"} body = {"model": M, "state": None, "images": [f"http://127.0.0.1:{srv.server_port}/x.png"], "questions": {"q1": q, "q2": q}} r = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(URL + "/v1/systemone", json.dumps(body).encode(), {"Content-Type": "application/json"}))) print("image GETs:", len(gets), "| P(red) q1 =", round(r["answers"]["q1"]["noul"], 3), "q2 =", round(r["answers"]["q2"]["noul"], 3)) ``` Observed (d1-3B): `image GETs: 2 | P(red) q1 = 0.986 q2 = 0.02`. Expected: `image GETs: 1` and the same answer for both questions.
### 3. Images above 1 MP give different answers from `system_one()` d1's `runner.py` shrinks every picture to at most 1024×1024 px (bicubic) before the processor; here it goes in as sent, so the tile grid and the pixels differ. Same commit as 2 (`LiquidStrategy.max_image_pixels`).
Repro, vllm serve LiquidAI/d1-3B --port 18676, img/cat03.jpg = Wikimedia Commons Cat03.jpg ```python # Server: vllm serve LiquidAI/d1-3B --port 18676 # The same photo sent as-is (1600x1598) and downscaled to 1 MP the way d1's runner.cap_pixels does. # model.system_one() always sees the 1 MP version, so only the second row matches the reference. import base64, io, json, math, os, sys, urllib.request from PIL import Image URL = f"http://127.0.0.1:{os.environ.get('PORT', '18676')}/v1/systemone" im = Image.open(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "img/cat03.jpg").convert("RGB") s = math.sqrt(1024 * 1024 / (im.width * im.height)) for tag, pic in [("as sent ", im), ("1MP-capped", im.resize((int(im.width * s), int(im.height * s)), Image.Resampling.BICUBIC))]: b = io.BytesIO(); pic.save(b, "PNG") body = {"model": "LiquidAI/d1-3B", "state": None, "images": ["data:image/png;base64," + base64.b64encode(b.getvalue()).decode()], "questions": {"indoor": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Is the photo taken indoors?"}}} r = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(URL, json.dumps(body).encode(), {"Content-Type": "application/json"}))) print(tag, pic.size, "P(indoor) =", round(r["answers"]["indoor"]["noul"], 4), "input_tokens =", r["usage"]["input_tokens"]) ``` Observed: as sent `P(indoor) = 0.1824`, 2578 tokens; capped `0.0953`, 1293 tokens. Expected: `system_one()` on the same file gives `0.0953` with 1293 tokens. In fp32 a 3840×2880 photo flips a yes/no answer (0.454 vs 0.551).
### 4. A one-letter option name that is several tokens fails with a `max()` error `"丙".isalpha()` is True, so 丙 becomes a code; 丙 and " 丙" are both multi-token, the group is `[]`, and the check (L305) compares `[]` with `ids[:1] == []` and passes. Fix (one line, `not ids or`): https://github.com/simon-veitner-redhat/vllm/commit/fee6ea22a6027cd228fc64d8a54f28efdf1c6c51
Repro, vllm serve LiquidAI/d1-3B --port 18676 ```bash # 丙 is one letter (isalpha) but two d1 tokens -> empty label group. curl -s -w '\nHTTP %{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:${PORT:-18676}/v1/systemone -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"LiquidAI/d1-3B","state":"Average quality.","questions":{"g":{"type":"choice","instructions":"Grade?","criteria":{"甲":"good","丙":"average"}}}}' ``` Observed: `400 "max() iterable argument is empty"`. Expected: the intended `400 "label '丙' is not one distinct token for this model"` (`system_one()` answers, using fallback code `A`).
### 5. `confidence` does not match `system_one()` The reference returns `probs[best]`; here it is `probs[top] * label_mass`, with `label_mass` summing every pooled variant. Picks and probabilities match; `confidence` is 0.004–0.020 lower on d1. Keeping one definition across models seems fine; the commit narrows the docs claim to picks and probabilities: https://github.com/simon-veitner-redhat/vllm/commit/37609180281ecb0079c9c9b833b1c0cc5bf169e3
Repro, vllm serve LiquidAI/d1-3B --port 18676 ```bash # The reference's choice confidence is max(probabilities); vLLM returns max(probabilities) * label_mass. curl -s http://127.0.0.1:${PORT:-18676}/v1/systemone -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"'${MODEL:-LiquidAI/d1-3B}'","state":"I was charged twice this month, please refund one of them.","questions":{"team":{"type":"choice","instructions":"Which team should handle this?","criteria":{"billing":"Charges, refunds, invoices","technical":"App or site faults","fraud":"Suspected unauthorised use"}}}}' \ | jq -c '{confidence: .answers.team.confidence, max_prob: ([.answers.team.probabilities[]]|max), label_mass: .diagnostics.team.label_mass, max_prob_x_mass: (([.answers.team.probabilities[]]|max) * .diagnostics.team.label_mass)}' ``` Observed: `{"confidence":0.97587,"max_prob":0.98423,"label_mass":0.99150}`. Expected (`system_one()`, same input): `confidence 0.98286`, its max probability.
### Run-to-run variance (fixed separately) Under concurrent load a label's bf16 logit moves by one step, so near-ties flip: the Japanese case picks English in about half of loaded runs. Computing the lm_head in fp32 removes this at no measured cost (322 vs 324 req/s at 32 in flight), but `--hf-overrides '{"head_dtype": "float32"}'` is ignored for multimodal models today; I will send that as a separate [Bugfix] PR. Until then `--hf-overrides '{"text_config": {"head_dtype": "float32"}}'` works.
Repro, vllm serve LiquidAI/d1-3B --port 18676 ```python # Server: vllm serve LiquidAI/d1-3B --port 18676 (bf16, default prefix caching) # The PR's Japanese case asked alone, then 32 times mixed with 32 other requests, 32 in flight. # Batch shape moves one label logit by one bf16 step: Japanese 0.3985 / English 0.3744 becomes # a 0.3837 tie, and argmax picks English. import collections, json, os, random, urllib.request from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor URL = f"http://127.0.0.1:{os.environ.get('PORT', '18676')}/v1/systemone" LANG = {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Which language is the message in?", "criteria": {"English": None, "Japanese": None, "Chinese": None}} JA = {"model": "LiquidAI/d1-3B", "state": {"message": "注文した商品がまだ届きません。返金してください。"}, "questions": {"lang": LANG}} def other(i): # a different request with a random-length state return {"model": "LiquidAI/d1-3B", "state": "refund order crash " * random.Random(i).choice([5, 50, 300]), "questions": {"d": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Angry?"}}} def ask(body): r = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(URL, json.dumps(body).encode(), {"Content-Type": "application/json"}))) a = r["answers"].get("lang") return a and (a["choice"], round(a["probabilities"]["Japanese"], 4), round(a["probabilities"]["English"], 4)) print("alone:", ask(JA)) jobs = [JA] * 32 + [other(i) for i in range(32)] random.Random(0).shuffle(jobs) with ThreadPoolExecutor(32) as ex: print("mixed:", collections.Counter(a for a in ex.map(ask, jobs) if a)) ``` Observed: `alone: ('Japanese', 0.3985, 0.3744)`, `mixed: Counter({('Japanese', 0.3985, 0.3744): 17, ('English', 0.3837, 0.3837): 15})`. Expected: all 32 equal to the answer asked alone (with the fp32 head, all 32 pick Japanese).
